standard.title: Interpret and predict economic impacts
standard.description: interpret information and data, explaining economic and business issues, trends and economic cause-and-effect relationships, and make predictions about consumer and financial impacts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can interpret information and data, explain economic and business issues, trends and cause-and-effect relationships, and make predictions at Year 9 level (AC9HE9S03). They have practised interpreting single-variable economic data, identifying trends and articulating cause-and-effect logic. Y10 builds on this with multi-variable data, more complex trend interpretation and more explicit prediction reasoning.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information and data to explain economic and business issues, trends and cause-and-effect relationships, and make reasoned predictions about consumer and financial impacts.

nodes.label: Explaining economic issues from data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret information to explain the nature, extent and importance of an economic or business issue.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret a provided data source about an economic issue and explain in at least two sentences what the data shows about the nature or extent of the issue.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret information to explain the nature, extent and importance of an economic or business issue — for example, the relationship between standards of living, infant mortality and access to health services; explain what the data reveals and why the issue matters.
wider: Interpret data about a complex multi-dimensional issue (e.g. housing affordability involving income, interest rates, housing supply and geographic distribution) and explain the interaction between factors
Evaluate how different data sources on the same issue can support different interpretations, and explain what this means for evidence-based decision-making
Investigate a global economic issue (e.g. supply chain disruption, climate-related economic risk) using international data and explain its implications for Australia
nodes.hinge_reason: If students cannot move from data to explanation — from 'this is what the data shows' to 'this is what it means about the issue' — they cannot produce the analytical outputs the descriptor requires. Trend identification without interpretation is a persistent failure mode.

response_modes.reason: Make the explanation move explicit: what does this data show → what does this mean about the issue → why does this matter? Students who stay at description need scaffolding to take the interpretive step.

success_criteria: States what a piece of data shows about an economic issue (description)
Explains what this means about the nature or extent of the issue (interpretation beyond description)

nodes.label: Interpreting multi-variable trends
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret multi-variable data to analyse trends over time, explaining reasons for changes and what the trend reveals about economic conditions.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret a provided multi-variable dataset (e.g. two indicators over time) and identify the trend and at least one reason for a change in direction.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret multi-variable data to analyse trends in economic activity over time — for example, trends in government health and education expenditure; explain reasons for changes in the trend and what the pattern reveals about priorities or conditions.
wider: Analyse an economic trend using three or more variables to identify leading and lagging relationships (e.g. how business investment precedes employment growth by 6–12 months)
Compare trends across two countries for the same economic variable and explain divergence or convergence over a significant period
Evaluate how a trend visualisation (e.g. a time series chart) can be presented to emphasise different interpretations, and what this means for data literacy

response_modes.reason: Practise multi-variable trend interpretation across different economic domains — government spending, employment, trade, household income. Fluency requires repeated application.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-variable trend analysis across different economic domains (fiscal, labour, trade, social) provides rich transferable practice. Students who become fluent with varied datasets develop genuine economic data literacy.
success_criteria: Correctly identifies the trend shown in a multi-variable dataset
Provides at least one plausible reason for a change in direction in the trend, supported by the data

nodes.label: Cause-and-effect analysis
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse causes and effects of an economic issue — explaining why the issue arises and what its consequences are for individuals, businesses or the broader economy.
nodes.minimum_width: For one economic issue, state at least one cause and one effect, explaining the connection between them.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse the causes and effects of an economic issue on individuals or businesses — for example, the reasons for and implications of government intervention in the economy to improve living standards; explain the chain of causation and identify who is affected and how.
wider: Map a multi-step causal chain (e.g. rising inflation → RBA cash rate increase → higher mortgage repayments → reduced consumer spending → slower growth) and evaluate where the chain might break
Analyse how the same economic cause produces different effects on different groups (e.g. rising interest rates affect renters, mortgage-holders and savers differently)
Investigate an economic issue where the cause-and-effect relationship is contested and evaluate competing explanations using evidence
nodes.hinge_reason: Cause-and-effect reasoning is the core analytical demand of this descriptor. Students who can describe trends but cannot explain why they happen — or what happens as a result — cannot produce the causal analysis the descriptor requires.

response_modes.reason: Build causal chains explicitly: cause → mechanism → effect. The mechanism step is where students most often default to assertion. Modelling multi-step chains with identifiable mechanisms is the key scaffold.
Apply causal analysis to varied economic issues — government intervention, consumer decisions, trade — so students generalise the analytical move rather than memorising one causal chain.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Causal analysis applied to diverse economic issues (fiscal policy, labour market, trade, household finance) develops deep analytical transferability. Multi-group effect analysis and contested causation add genuine intellectual richness.
success_criteria: States a cause-and-effect relationship for an economic issue with at least one intermediate mechanism explained
Identifies at least one group affected by the effect and explains why they are affected

nodes.label: Making predictions about consumer and financial impacts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse trends and cause-and-effect relationships to make reasoned predictions about who will be affected and how, with reference to economic evidence.
nodes.minimum_width: Based on a provided trend or causal analysis, make one prediction about consumer or financial impacts and explain the reasoning behind it.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse trends to make predictions about who will be affected and how — for example, trends in productivity and implications for businesses; explain the reasoning underpinning the prediction and acknowledge conditions under which it might not hold.
wider: Make a conditional prediction — 'if [economic condition], then [consumer/financial impact], because [mechanism]' — and evaluate the quality of the prediction against evidence of what actually happened
Compare predictions made by different economic commentators about the same trend and evaluate whose reasoning was most sound in retrospect
Investigate how businesses use economic trend data to make investment and staffing predictions and evaluate how prediction quality affects business outcomes

response_modes.reason: Prediction integrates interpretation, trend analysis and causal reasoning into a single forward-looking claim. This is the descriptor's full demand — the ability to use economic evidence to reason about likely future impacts.

success_criteria: Makes a specific prediction about consumer or financial impacts connected to a named trend or causal relationship
Provides explicit reasoning for the prediction — the mechanism that links the trend to the predicted outcome
